title: John Paul II Visits the Man Who Shot Him
text:
On May 13, 1981, Pope John Paul II was riding through St. Peter's Square in Rome when a young Turkish gunman, Mehmet Ali Agca, fired at him. The Pope was hit in the abdomen and hand and lost a great deal of blood. He survived after hours of surgery. Agca was caught on the spot and sentenced to life imprisonment.

A few days after the shooting, from his hospital bed, the Pope asked people to pray for the brother who had shot him, whom he said he had sincerely forgiven.

On December 27, 1983, John Paul II went to Rebibbia prison in Rome and met Agca in his cell. Photographers recorded the two men sitting close together, the Pope holding Agca's hand as they spoke quietly for about twenty minutes. Afterward the Pope told reporters that what they had said would remain a secret between them, and that he had spoken to Agca as a brother he had pardoned.

The Pope kept in touch with Agca's family. In 2000 Italy pardoned Agca, with the Vatican's support, and sent him to Turkey to serve a sentence for an earlier murder.
lesson: Forgiveness is a choice that belongs to you, not to the person who hurt you. It can be offered without waiting for them to deserve it.
people: Pope John Paul II, Mehmet Ali Agca
source: Contemporary press reports and photographs of the prison visit (December 27 to 28, 1983); George Weigel, Witness to Hope (1999)
